name: Pow-R-Line 1a
status: Legacy; renewal parts still listed April 2021. Superseded by PRL1X (Pow-R-Line Xpert, introduced 2020; time line shows PRL1X/2X/3X/4X from May 2020)
era: Introduced October 1996 (Cutler-Hammer); part of 'Pow-R-Line C' line introduced 1993
overview: Cutler-Hammer/Eaton 240 Vac lighting & appliance panelboard on a 20 in wide box, neutral located in the side gutter. Branch QUICKLAG breakers mount horizontally on factory connector strips (bolt-on 1C96608 or plug-on 2C11642 assemblies); mains, sub-feed breakers and main/sub-feed/through-feed lugs mount vertically on KB/KL connector kits. Fully rated 10/22 kA, series rated to 200 kA at 240 Vac. Suitable for service entrance when specified (PRLSEB barrier kits, 4180B62 bonding jumper). Note: Eaton literature also uses the umbrella name 'Pow-R-Line C' for Series C breaker panelboards; that name is not unique to PRL1a and is also the name of the PRLC switchboard.

name: Pow-R-Line 2a
status: Legacy; renewal parts listed April 2021; superseded by PRL2X
era: Introduced October 1996
overview: 480Y/277 Vac lighting panelboard sharing the PRL1a chassis architecture (20 in box, gutter neutral, KB vertical kits, KL lug kits, 1C96638 deadfront). Branch breakers are GHB-family bolt-ons on 1C96609 horizontal connector assemblies. GHB main breaker is horizontally mounted; all other mains vertical. Fully rated 14 kA at 480Y/277, series rated 22-150 kA.

name: Pow-R-Line 3a
status: Legacy; renewal parts listed April 2021; superseded by PRL3X. Deadfront/filler hardware changed for panels built after April 2019 (distributor wording)
era: Introduced March 1994
overview: Power distribution panelboard on a 20 in wide box with the neutral in the main (top/bottom) gutter. Chassis height measured in X units (1X = 1.38 in); deadfront is a rail-and-end-cover frame (6559C59) with individual device covers. Branch devices are horizontally mounted on bus-stab connector kits that ship with their own device deadfront cover. Max 200 A on any one connector.

name: Pow-R-Line 3E
status: Current in June 2020 catalog
era: Shown in January 2018 and June 2020 catalogs
overview: Compact distribution panelboard variant built around Eaton EG-frame (Series G E-frame) bolt-on branch breakers up to 125 A. Not covered by the renewal-parts guides found; no PRL3E connector kits identified.

name: Pow-R-Line 4 (PRL4B breaker / PRL4F fusible / PRL4D drawout)
aliases: PRL-4; PRL4; PRL4B; PRL4D; PRL4F; PRL4X; Pow-R-Line 4; Pow-R-Line 4B; Pow-R-Line 4D; Pow-R-Line 4F
status: Legacy; renewal parts listed April 2021; superseded by PRL4X/PRL4DX (PRL4F continues in Xpert catalog)
era: PRL4B/F introduced October 1987
overview: Heavy distribution panelboard in 24, 36 or 44 in wide boxes (BX2457..BX4490), neutral in main gutter, vertical bus with branch devices horizontally mounted single or twin on KPRL4* connector kits measured in X units (1X = 1.38 in). Front is a vented cover assembly (two side rails, top/bottom vented covers, 6574C74) plus individual device covers and blank covers (6554C01/6554C02). Density-rated bus option required for some 100% rated breaker kits.

name: Pow-R-Line Xpert 1X
status: Current
era: Introduced 2020 (time line: May 2020)
overview: Pow-R-Line Xpert successor to PRL1a. Shares PRL1a horizontal branch assemblies (1C96608/2C11642/1C96609), lug kits (KL*), neutral/ground assemblies and deadfronts, but vertical main/sub-feed connector kits are for Power Defense frames (KB..2T/B, KB..34, KB..36). Each branch connector rated up to 140 A total by breaker rating.

name: Pow-R-Line Xpert 2X
status: Current
era: Introduced 2020
overview: Pow-R-Line Xpert successor to PRL2a; parts tables shared with PRL1X/PRL1a/PRL2a in RP01400001E.

name: Pow-R-Line Xpert 3X
status: Current
era: Introduced 2020
overview: Successor to PRL3a; same 20 in box and X-unit chassis concept. Uses KPRL3X* connector kits and 42C80xx deadfront covers (PDG2 replaces F-frame).

name: Pow-R-Line Xpert 4X (incl. PRL4DX, PRL4F)
status: Current
era: Introduced 2020
overview: Successor to PRL4B; renewal parts (blank covers, vented covers, KPRL4X/KPRL4* connector kits, retrofit kits) are listed jointly for PRL4X and PRL4 in RP01400001E (2021).

name: Pow-R-Line column-type (PRL1a-LX, PRL2a-LX, PRL1X-LX, PRL2X-LX)
aliases: PRL1a-LX; PRL2a-LX; PRL1X-LX; PRL2X-LX; column panelboard
status: Legacy (a) / current (X)
era: PRL1a/2a-LX introduced December 1997
overview: Narrow column-width lighting panels (box YSC969-YSC990, trims LTC/LTCD). Renewal parts listed are boxes and trims only.

name: Westinghouse Pow-R-Line 1 / Pow-R-Line 2 (vintage)
aliases: POW-R-LINE; PRL1; PRL1-LX; PRL2; Pow-R-Line 1; Pow-R-Line 2
status: Obsolete; limited renewal parts (Sumter Aftermarket Center) per Feb 2013 guide
era: Westinghouse panelboards manufactured after 1988 (1988 redesign for Series C)
overview: Original Westinghouse Pow-R-Line lighting panelboards on 20 in wide boxes (YS20xx, 5.75 in deep) with gutter neutral; trims LT20xxS/F. Branch connector kits hold two sets of A/B/C connectors for 12 poles, silver-plated copper suitable for Cu or Al bus, max 140 A per connector. Branch deadfronts 5156C10 (PRL1) / 5156C09 (PRL2).

name: Westinghouse Pow-R-Line 3 (vintage)
status: Obsolete; limited renewal parts
era: Pre-1994 Westinghouse
overview: Westinghouse distribution panelboard, 20 in box, main-gutter neutral, trims LTT20xxS/F. Eaton notes the PRL3 connector kits also fit Westinghouse panelboards WEB, WCA, WEHB, WFB and HWFB.

name: Westinghouse CDP / HCDP distribution panelboard
aliases: CDP; CDP/HCDP; CPD; HCDP; Westinghouse CDP
status: Obsolete; retrofit and connector kits available from Sumter Plant Aftermarket
era: Westinghouse power panelboard; with FDP, encompassed most Westinghouse MCCBs for more than 34 years (to 1988 redesign); Cutler-Hammer also built CDP under supply agreement
overview: Westinghouse distribution panelboard in 30-50 in wide boxes with chassis rails and vertical chassis bus, 3.50 in phase-to-phase bus centre-lines (switch kits). Series C retrofit kits (KCDP+breaker catalog no.) use same X space as original breakers; KD onto LB connectors requires TAD3 adapter.

name: Westinghouse FDP fusible distribution panelboard
status: Obsolete; switch retrofit/connector kits available
era: Vintage Westinghouse
overview: Westinghouse fusible distribution panelboard (30-50 in wide). FDPW/FDPB switch connector kits KFDP* require 3.50 in bus spacing.

name: Pow-R-Line 5P plug-on distribution panelboard
status: Discontinued (dropped from 2021 renewal parts; in 2009 and 2017 editions)
era: Introduced August 1995
overview: Plug-on distribution panelboard with single-bus (30 in box) or double-bus (48 in box) chassis; breakers supplied as complete adapter units (catalog 5P...).

name: Pow-R-Command lighting control panelboard
status: Current (Pow-R-Command E series in 2020 catalog)
era: Introduced March 1996
overview: Lighting control panelboard based on PRL3a/3X chassis; renewal parts (connector kits, grounds, SE kits, deadfronts, trim locks) are per PRL3X/PRL3a section.

name: Pow-R-Line C switchboard
aliases: Pow-R-Line C; POW-R-LINE C; PRL-C; Pow-R-Line C switchboard; Type 1 Pow-R-Line C
status: current (listed in April 2018 consulting guide)
era: Introduced late 1980s (1988) by Westinghouse as successor to WF/WRP; built in Sumter SC and Visalia CA; current Eaton product
overview: Eaton (originally Westinghouse) Class II service-distribution switchboard, UL 891 / NEMA PB-2, front- or rear-access, with individually mounted mains and group-mounted feeder chassis. Evolved from the Westinghouse WF/WRP St. Louis switchboard when the design moved to Sumter SC and Visalia CA in 1988 with the introduction of Series C breakers. Distribution chassis are laid out in X units (1X = 1-3/8 in) on 38X or 50X vertical panel space in 36 in or 45 in wide structures; device X requirements (EHD 1-3X, FD 2-3X, JD 3X, KD 4X, LD/MDL/ND 6X) parallel the PRL4 panelboard chassis. Vol 12 states breaker provisions 'are available for all ratings of the Pow-R-Line C designs including all parts required to complete the cell', but no PRLC-specific provision kit catalog numbers were found in public documents (factory/Sumter quoted).

name: Westinghouse WF/WRP switchboard
aliases: WF; WRP; Type WF; Type WRP; WF/WRP switchboard
status: discontinued (superseded by Pow-R-Line C)
era: Introduced 1955 by Westinghouse, St. Louis MO; design transferred 1988 to Sumter SC and Visalia CA as Pow-R-Line C
successor: Pow-R-Line C switchboard (new PRLC match/lineup structures can connect to existing WF/WRP)
overview: Westinghouse St. Louis Class II switchboard. Type WF = front access (rear flush), Type WRP = rear access (front and rear flush). Feeders were panel-mounted molded-case breakers or FDP fusible switches — the same device family used in CDP/FDP panelboards. Eaton's Sumter aftermarket center offers 'retrofit kits for WF and WRP distribution sections' and 'connector kits for WF and WRP distribution sections' (RP01400002E p.20), and Vol 12 says provisions/connectors are available for most ratings of WF/WRP; no catalog numbers published.

name: Cutler-Hammer Type ES switchboard
status: discontinued (Vol 12 lists as legacy; new PRLC can connect via transition section)
era: Introduced 1991 by Cutler-Hammer as replacement for their version of WF/WRP; Mullenbach (1962) heritage; used exclusively Westinghouse MCCBs
overview: Cutler-Hammer branded service distribution switchboard using Westinghouse molded-case breakers under the 1960s supply agreement. Existing ES lineups can be extended with new Pow-R-Line C structures through a transition section.

name: Pow-R-Line i switchboard
aliases: Pow-R-Line i; PRL i; Pow-R-Line I
status: current (2018 consulting guide)
era: Evolved in 1991 from Asheville 'Pow-R-I' (itself from WRI); built in Sumter SC
overview: Rear-access, front- and rear-aligned UL 891 switchboard with individually compartmentalized feeder devices (not group-mounted). Included here for lineage; branch hardware is device-specific compartments rather than group-mounted connector kits.

name: Pow-R-Line CS switchboard
status: current (Canadian market; manual IB015002EN effective Nov 2021)
overview: Eaton Canada switchboard line documented by instruction manual IB015002EN (Nov 2021). Manual gives bus-joint torque table (Appendix A). No branch kit catalog numbers found.

name: Integrated Facility System switchboard
status: current (2018 consulting guide)
overview: Free-standing front-access UL 891 switchboard that integrates standard panelboards, dry-type transformers and other equipment in 'cells'; used with Type 1 Pow-R-Line C switchboard sections.

name: Westinghouse WEB/WCA/WEHB/WFB/HWFB panelboards
aliases: WEB; WCA; WEHB; WFB; HWFB; WGB; WGHB
status: discontinued; replacement panelboard type PRL3a (WGB/WGHB -> PRL2a)
overview: Westinghouse 1937-1988 era panelboards named for their branch breaker (E-frame, CA, F-frame, G-frame). PRL3 connector kits (KPRL3FD, KPRL3ED, KPRL3CA) fit WEB, WCA, WEHB, WFB and HWFB.

name: Westinghouse NLAB lighting panelboard
aliases: NLAB; NLAB-LX; NLAB-AB; NLAB-ABH; NPLAB; NQB; NQP; NQC
status: discontinued; connectors not available; replace panelboard with PRL1a (NLAB, NPLAB, NQB, NQP, NQC), PRL1aLX (NLAB-LX), PRL3a (NLAB-AB/ABH)
era: Westinghouse panelboards manufactured between 1937 and 1988
overview: Westinghouse plug-in/bolt-on lighting panelboards for Quicklag-type Q breakers. Vol 12 flags 'connectors not available' for this group; replacement is a new PRL1a/PRL3a interior. CDP/FDP/NQB trim clamp 414A380G02 still applies to NQB.

name: Westinghouse NAB / NA1B / NH1B / NDP / NEB panelboards
aliases: NAB; NA1B; NH1B; NHB; NDP; NHDP; NEB; NHEB; ABH; A2B
status: discontinued; connectors not available; replacement panelboard PRL3a (NAB, NA1B, NDP, NEB, NHDP, NHEB, ABH) or PRL2a (NH1B); panelboard-only replacement breaker REH/RHFA
overview: Westinghouse 1937-1988 lighting/appliance and distribution panelboards using E-family plug/bolt breakers. Branch breakers replaced by 'panelboard only' R-prefix breakers (REH, RHF, RHFA) supplied with mounting hardware; connector kits not available. The scope term 'NHB' is not used in Vol 12; nearest OEM designations are NH1B and NHEB.

name: Type BR loadcenter
aliases: BR; Type BR; Bryant BR; Challenger BR
status: current (Eaton Type BR)
era: Made by Westinghouse's Bryant subsidiary, Bridgeport CT, until 1989 (Westinghouse and Bryant nameplates); Westinghouse bought Challenger Electric 1988, redesigned the product and moved production to Jackson MS; from 1995 Eaton moved all loadcenter production to Lincoln IL
overview: 1-in-per-pole plug-on residential/light-commercial loadcenter family with Westinghouse/Bryant/Challenger lineage. Vol 12 Tab 5 lists replacement main/subfeed lug blocks, filler plates, interlocks and handle accessories.

name: Eaton / Cutler-Hammer Type CH and Type BR panelboard retrofit kits (reuse of existing box)
aliases: Retro Size A-E; RA/RB/RC/RD/RE/RAA retrofit kits; Lincoln Flex Center retrofit
status: Unknown whether still offered as standard kits; Eaton continues custom retrofit interiors via Flex Centers
era: Introduced as 'new' offering in undated Eaton Electrical guide (Eaton Electrical brand used c.2003-2008)
overview: Eaton/Cutler-Hammer standardized retrofit kits for re-using an existing (any-manufacturer, e.g. FPE or Zinsco) flush panel box: a cover assembly (field-drilled picture frame + trim) and a field-adjustable interior assembly with riser accommodating 4-6 in box depth (3.5-5.25 in for size AA). Kits are selected by existing box height into Retro Size groups A (21-30 in, cover 33x24), B (29-36, 40x24), C (34-41, 43x24), D (37-45, 47x24), E (45-54, 56x24), plus AA for boxes 14.5-20.5 in high (covers 19x13 or 21x16). Interiors are 'UL recognized under UL67'; whether the installed assembly in a foreign box is listed is debated (forum), so AHJ/field evaluation may be required. Hosted by InspectAPedia as an FPE Stab-Lok replacement option.

name: Challenger distribution panelboards (PM4a / PM4b)
status: Obsolete (Challenger acquired by Westinghouse late 1980s/1994; Eaton from 1994); kits available as surplus
overview: Challenger Electrical Equipment (formed c.1981 from GTE-Sylvania's distribution business, Jackson MS) built distribution panelboards annotated 'PM4a' and 'PM4b' in relectric's catalogue. Mounting kits follow the pattern C<frame>D<n>K (twin) / C<frame>DS<n>K (single), with 'B' variants (e.g., CED4BK) annotated PM4b. Eaton-numbered KPRL4C*/KPRL4AC*/KPRL4BC* kits appear to adapt Challenger breakers into Pow-R-Line 4 style interiors. Coded EAT per lineage table.

name: FPE CDP distribution panelboard (single-hole bus)
status: Obsolete; aftermarket/replacement kits and recertified breakers still sold by FPE-successor (Circuit Breaker Sales / fpeparts.com) and surplus dealers
era: FPE commercial distribution panelboard line; obsolete. Exact production years not documented in sources found.
successor: No direct OEM successor. Parts support: Federal Pacific Equipment -> Circuit Breaker Sales (fpeparts.com); aftermarket kits NEF1K/NEJ1K/NFJ1K/NJL1K (PCS) replace OEM KCDP1C-KCDP4C.
overview: FPE CDP is a commercial/industrial distribution panelboard using a 'single hole bus' (per Superbreakers description) onto which pairs of N-frame bolt-on molded-case breakers are mounted with OEM bus connection ('link') kits KCDP1C through KCDP5C, one kit per breaker frame family. Each kit (per Breaker King) includes screws, brackets and a deadfront cover plate and mounts two breakers (twin). Aftermarket equivalents NEF1K, NEJ1K, NFJ1K, NJL1K are cross-referenced to the OEM kits. NN-frame switches (e.g., NN633120NA) are also described as fitting CDP panelboards.

name: FPE BDP distribution panelboard (double-hole bus)
aliases: BDP panel board; BDP Spectra bolt-on (as listed by Superbreakers - likely erroneous)
status: Obsolete; OEM-numbered kits KBDP1C-KBDP5C and aftermarket NEF3K/NEJ3K/NJL3K still traded
overview: FPE BDP is a distribution panelboard with a 'double hole bus' (Superbreakers) using twin bus-connection kits KBDP1C-KBDP5C per breaker frame. Breaker King sells PCS aftermarket assemblies NEF3K/NEJ3K/NJL3K replacing KBDP1C/KBDP2C/KBDP4C. Superbreakers labels KBDP1C as 240 V 100 A for 'BDP Spectra Bolt-on' panelboards - the 'Spectra' wording appears to be a listing error (Spectra is a GE name).

name: FPE FDP fusible distribution panelboard / QMQB switchboard
aliases: QMQB panelboard; QMQB switchboard; Federal Pacific QMQB
status: Obsolete; QMQB switches and KFDP/KQB strap/link kits still traded as recertified/new-surplus
overview: FDP is FPE's fusible distribution panelboard family built around QMQB bolt-on fusible switch units ('used for QMQB and FDP style panel boards and switchgear distribution systems'). Switch units connect to the vertical bus through KFDP-series link/strap kits (KFDP2C, 3C, 4C (200 A), 46C (400 A), 66C (600 A), 7C (1200 A), plus D/S/V variants KFDPD16C, KFDPS16C, KFDPD26C, KFDPS26C, KFDPV7C) and KQB-series kits (KQB3C 15-100 A, KQB4C, KQB46C, KQB66C, KQB86C 700-800 A).

name: FPE NDP panelboard
status: Obsolete
overview: NDP is an FPE panelboard type supported by twin mounting strap kits NDPNE and NDPNEJ (relectric). fpeparts.com also lists 'NHDP panel board kit' and 'LDP panel board kit' families; relationship of NDP/NHDP/LDP to CDP/BDP not documented.

name: FPE NA1B / NH1B lighting and appliance panelboards
aliases: NAIB; NH1B; NHIB; NA-type panel; NH-type panel; NAB; NHB
status: Obsolete
overview: NA1B ('NAIB') and NH1B ('NHIB') are FPE lighting/appliance panelboard types. A used kit KCDP-1A is labelled 'For NE/NEF frame circuit breakers, for NH1B/NA1B type panels, for (2) 3 pole breakers'. relectric lists NAIB-NEF 'NE/NEF twin kit for NA1B panel' and Superbreakers lists KNA1B1C lug kit. fpeparts.com lists 'NAIB panel board kit' and 'NHIB panel board kit'. By analogy with FPE breaker naming (NA=Stab-Lok 120/240 plug-in; NE/NEF=bolt-on 240/480 V) NA1B is likely the 120/240 or 208Y/120 panel and NH1B the 480Y/277 panel, but this is unverified.

name: FPE NBLP / NQLP bolt-on lighting panelboards
status: Obsolete; Schneider Electric states it no longer offers replacement breakers for Federal Pacific switchboards/panelboards
overview: NBLP panelboards take NB-type bolt-on Stab-Lok-style breakers (Schneider FAQ snippet; Superbreakers NB100 'installs into Federal Pacific NB and NBLP panelboards'). NQ breakers are described as fitting NBLP and NQLP panelboards. Federal Pioneer (Canadian FPE subsidiary, sold to Schneider Canada in 1988) used the same Stab-Lok NB/NBLP nomenclature; that lineage is coded SQD in this catalogue.

name: FPE switchboards (N-frame bolt-on / NM-NN-NP / Fusematic)
status: Obsolete; recertified NJL/NJJ/NM/NP breakers and NN switches sold for legacy FPE switchboards
overview: FPE switchboards used N-frame bolt-on breakers (NJL 'designed for direct installation into legacy Federal Pacific switchboards and panelboards that accept N-frame bolt-on breakers'), larger NM (400-800 A with trip units NM031400/500/600/800, lugs NM34/NM36/NM38) and NP frames (to 1600 A), and the Fusematic line (XF breakers, XJL current limiters). Group-mounting hardware for switchboards not identified beyond the panelboard KCDP/KBDP kits.

name: A-Series Lighting Panelboards (Types AL, AQ, AE/AS, AD / AD Plus, Lighting Control Panel, Pro-Stock AQU/AEU)
aliases: A Series; A-Series II; AQ; AE; AS; AL; AD; AD Plus; AQF; AEF; Pro-Stock
status: current as of BuyLog 07/2014
overview: GE's lighting/appliance panelboard platform. Symmetrical 20 in wide x 5.81 in deep galvanized boxes with removable endwalls, branch-bus direct connection and captive branch hardware. Type letter indicates breaker family: AL = plug-in Q-line, AQ = bolt-on Q-line (THQB), AE = bolt-on E-frame (TEY) 480Y/277 V, AD = 600 V TED/SE/FB. Pro-Stock unassembled interiors (AQU/AEU) are completed with MB main breaker kits, ML main lug kits and NK neutral kits. Pages in the 2014 BuyLog are headed 'A-Series II' on the column-panel kit page.

name: A-Series Power Panelboards / A-Series II Power Panel (Types AQP, AEP, ADP; 'Type P & N')
aliases: AQP; AEP; ADP; A-Series II Powerpanel; AD/AE/AQ Type P & N Power Panel
status: current as of BuyLog 07/2014
overview: Power-panel version of the A-Series: 30 in wide x 8 in deep box, single-piece deadfront (no filler plates needed per catalog), up to 600 A branch device, staggered center-mounted SF/SG breakers. Field breaker kits ASPP6xxxx (DEH40150-DEH40158) are installed into 'Un-Specified Space' on the interior, bolting branch bases/straps to the main bus next to the crossbar and replacing a blank shield insert on the deadfront with a breaker-specific filler plate.

name: A-Series Column Panelboards (ALC, AQC, AEC)
overview: Narrow column-type A-Series panels (8.62 in wide x 5.81 in deep). ALC plug-in Q-line, AQC bolt-on THQB, AEC bolt-on TEY 15-80 A.

name: Spectra Series Power Panelboards (Plug-In interior type APN; Bolt-On interior type APNB)
aliases: Spectra; Spectra Series; SpectraRMS; APN; APNB; Spectra Bolt-On (SBO); Spectra Plug-In
status: Listed as current in 2014 BuyLog; a 2021/2022 ABB BuyLog TOC reportedly labels Spectra bolt-on mounting hardware 'obsoleted'
successor: ReliaGear neXT power panelboards (ABB) - inferred from ABB BuyLog placing 'Retrofit kit for Spectra panelboards' alongside ReliaGear neXT
overview: GE's power distribution panelboard. Two interior styles: APN plug-in (breakers bolt to AMC circuit breaker mounting modules that latch onto the interior rail and clip onto the bus; ADS fusible switch modules) and APNB bolt-on (breakers bolt to copper straps AMCB kits fastened with carriage bolts/antiturn clips to the vertical bus). Vertical space measured in X units (1X = 1-3/8 in). Box widths 27/31/36/40/44 in, APB boxes and APF fronts, AML main-lug modules, ANK/ANKN neutral kits, AEG ground kits. NOTE on 'APN': in GE nomenclature APN is the Spectra plug-in interior type code (APNB = bolt-on), while APN48/APN84/APN126 (A-Series) and APN49/APN99 (Spectra) are permanent circuit-number tab kits; no 'A-Series power panel' code APN was found.

name: Spectra Series Type SCP Plus panelboards
overview: Spectra-family power panel variant with its own ACB boxes (31 and 40 in wide x 11.5 in deep), ACF fronts, ACTMK/ACSMK mounting hardware kits (hardware + straps), ACTFPK/ACSFPK filler kits and ACTHK/ACSHK single-breaker hardware. Filler plates for SCP+ are to be ordered from the Houston equipment plant.

name: Type CCB and QMR power panelboards (legacy; listed under Spectra Series Power renewal parts)
status: Renewal parts still listed 2014; QMR fusible switches 'Limited availability. Obsolete when inventory depleted.'
overview: Older GE power panelboards. Breakers mount with copper strap kits suffixed DPK (dual/twin mount) or SPK (single mount) usable on Cu or Al main bus; device product number + suffix ordered as a unit. Replacement CCB fronts CBAxxxxS/F and boxes DASW/DACB; filler plates CCBFPx/QMRFPx. QMR used THFP fusible switches. CDP is named in the batch scope but no CDP-specific data was found.

name: NAB / NHB bolt-on panelboards (legacy)
status: discontinued (legacy); hardware sold as new-surplus
overview: Legacy GE bolt-on panelboard line. Only distributor evidence found (NHB150PK twin-mount hardware). No OEM document for NHB or NLAB located in this batch.

name: ReliaGear neXT Power Panelboards
overview: ABB's post-2018 power panelboard (doc 1SXU900191B0201, 2022). ABB states there is a single catalog number for all circuit breaker installation kits; that number was not found in accessible sources.

name: AV-Line switchboards (legacy)
overview: Legacy GE distribution switchboard; only surplus listings (800-1600 A, 208Y/120 to 480Y/277 V, Power Break mains) were found. No OEM document located.

name: Trumbull Electric (Plainville CT) panelboards and switches
status: Obsolete; forum states GE and Trumbull breakers share part numbers (e.g., TQL/THQL)
era: Trumbull Electric Mfg. Co., Plainville CT, labelled 'A General Electric Organization'; split-bus panels into early 1960s
overview: Trumbull Electric was GE's panelboard/switch maker before GE-branded distribution products; later Trumbull panels accept GE breakers per labels. Coded GEA per lineage. No Trumbull hardware part numbers were found.

name: Frank Adam Electric panelboards
status: Obsolete, rare
era: Company founded 1891 St. Louis; panels/breakers made through the 1950s (installed c.1900-1950, possibly to 1970); patents 1906-1965
successor: No known successor; West-coast business became Zinsmeyer Co. (1929/30s) -> Zinsco (1943)
overview: Frank Adam Electric Co. (St. Louis) made panelboards, fused switches and breakers from c.1900; its west-coast branch became Zinsco. Labels include PULFUZSW and KLAMPSWFUZ fused main panels and Fuselok switches. InspectAPedia reports some Frank Adam panelboards used Zinsco-type QSF units. A surplus 'FAM CU-NFJ hardware kit' suggests late Frank Adam panelboards accepted FPE NFJ breakers (unverified).

name: Wadsworth panelboards and breakers
status: Obsolete; reconditioned/NOS Wadsworth A- and B-series breakers sold by surplus dealers; Connecticut Electric replacements mentioned
era: Common 1950s-1960s; forum claims no Wadsworth breakers made since c.1970 (unsourced)
overview: Wadsworth Electric (Covington KY) made residential and light commercial panels and plug-in breakers; 3-pole A-series up to at least 90 A suggests 3-phase panelboards. No mounting hardware part numbers found.

name: Commander / CEB panels (Zinsco-type)
status: Obsolete; an electrician quoted by InspectAPedia says older Commander and CEB panels are 'really the same panel' as Sylvania/GTE-Sylvania (Zinsco design); newer Commander 200 A mains mounted differently
overview: Commander panels are reported (opinion only) to be Zinsco/Sylvania-design panels sold under another label; manufacturer identity unconfirmed.

name: Kinney panelboards
status: Company reportedly still in Elgin IL; legacy breaker support possibly via Eaton vintage products (forum)
overview: Kinney (Elgin, IL) panelboards appear in older commercial buildings; breaker type and lineage unverified. Lead only.

name: Type P1 (Revised P1)
aliases: Revised P1; New Revised P1; NextGen P1; P1...T; P1...N
status: current
era: Introduced 2015 per SpeedFax p.11-7 note ('Revised P1 was introduced in 2015'); p.11-11 table header says 'Revised P1 introduced 2014'
overview: Siemens 20in wide x 5.75in deep bolt-on lighting/appliance panelboard, 250A or 400A bus, split (cross-bussed) neutral at both ends of an open-ended bus. Field-convertible mains: main lug kits (MLK*) or horizontal main/subfeed strap kits (MBK*) through 250A, vertical 400A main. Catalog numbers end in T (feed-thru/subfeed space) or N (non-feed-thru, 6in shorter box). Revised P1 kits are not interchangeable with original P1, S1/S2 or SE panels.

name: Type P1 (original)
status: discontinued (kits still offered)
era: Pre-2014/2015 (replaced by Revised P1); listed in SPEEDFAX 2007-2008
overview: Original Siemens P1 lighting panelboard (pre-revision), 20in wide x 5.75in deep, main lug or main/subfeed strap kits through 400A. Subfeed space standard. Catalog numbers like Revised P1 but without the T suffix, up to 42 circuits. Kits for original P1 (MBKBL1, MBKED3, MBKQR3, MLKA3 etc.) are strap-only (breakers not included) and also fit 250A-max S1/S2 panels.

name: Type S1 / S2 lighting panelboards
aliases: S1; S2; Sentron S1; Sentron S2
status: discontinued; some kits available
overview: Earlier Siemens (Sentron-era) bolt-on lighting panelboards preceding P1/P2. SpeedFax states that all original P1 kits for 250A-and-below panels work in 250A-max S1/S2 panels; 400/600A S1/S2 use the SMBK* strap kits. Revised P1 kits will not work in S1/S2.

name: Type SE panelboard
status: discontinued
overview: Legacy Siemens panelboard type grouped with S1/S2 in SpeedFax replacement tables. SMBK* strap kits fit all SE panels; only AL 250A MLO kits (MLKA1/MLKA3) available for SE. Construction details unknown.

name: Type P2 panelboard
status: current
overview: Siemens bolt-on lighting/distribution panelboard with unit-space construction; branch devices installed via field strap kits (BBK*) in 3in or 6in increments; deadfront uses center strips (DFK*) and blank plates (DFFP3/DFFP6).

name: Type P3 panelboard
status: current
overview: Siemens 24in wide x 7.75in deep lighting/distribution panelboard sized like a lighting panel; unit-space construction with twin-mount strap kits (BBKB32 etc.), QJ/QR twin kits and 3VA52 twin kits (max 6 large-frame breakers in unit space).

name: Type P4 / S4 / Sentron SPP (10in deep) power panelboard
aliases: S4; SPP; Sentron SPP shallow; F1; FPP (10in)
status: current
overview: Siemens 10in-deep distribution (power) panelboard. Branch circuit breakers mount in unit space on 'Connecting Strap Kits' (S* series, e.g. SBL, SE6, SQR, SF6, SJ1, SL6) supplied without breaker; fusible branches use F6xx kits. Same strap kit family serves Type S4 and Sentron SPP shallow panels.

name: Type P5 / S5 / Sentron SPP deep (12.75in deep) power panelboard
aliases: S5; SPP deep; Sentron Deep; F2; FPP deep
status: current
overview: Siemens 12.75in-deep distribution panelboard. Branch connecting strap kits carry a 'D' suffix (SBLBD, SE6D, SF6D, SJ1D, SMND...). SpeedFax footnote: these kits also fit Types FCI, FCII, SB1 and SB2 switchboards.

name: Type SB1 / SB2 / SB3 distribution switchboards
aliases: SB1; SB2; SB3; SB4 (blank plates only)
status: current
overview: Siemens front-accessible distribution switchboards. Branch MCCBs mount in distribution sections via 'Connection Strap Kits' (same D-suffix kits as P5: SBLBD, SE6D, SF6D, SJ1D, SMND etc. plus S3VA*TD kits), unit space covered with 6FPB blank plates.

name: Series 5 / Series 6 CDP, VB5/VB6 panelboards and FC20 / FCI / FCII switchboards (ITE / Siemens-Allis heritage)
aliases: CDP-5; CDP-6; CDP6; SPP6; VB-5; VB-6; FC20; FC-20; FCI; FC-I; FCII; FC-II; FCRS; Class II
status: discontinued equipment; strap kits still catalogued (Canada)
era: Strap kits fit switchboards manufactured since 1974
overview: Legacy distribution panelboard and switchboard lines served by the Series 6 connecting strap kits (6E62, 6F62, 6JJ62, 6LL61...) and 6FPB blank plates. 2005 Siemens price list states these kits fit 'switchboards manufactured since 1974'. Equipment lineage (ITE/Gould-ITE/Siemens-Allis) for each type not confirmed in OEM documents in this batch.

name: Bulldog / ITE Pushmatic panelboards and Electri-Centers (incl. 3-phase versions)
status: Obsolete; replacement breakers from Connecticut Electric (UBIP series, 1-2 pole 120/240 V, 10 kAIC ETL) and new-old-stock ITE/Siemens Pushmatic; 3-pole 208Y/120 replacements reported back-ordered/unavailable
era: Bulldog Electric Products Co. (Detroit; patents from 1934-36, panelboard patent US 2,428,320 of 1947); installed mainly 1950-1970; ITE (Gould) purchase stated 1976 (forum says 1950s - conflicting); Siemens c.1982-84
successor: Siemens owns Pushmatic trademark (per InspectAPedia/forum); no current panelboard
overview: Bulldog Pushmatic panels use push-button (not toggle) bolt-on breakers, grease-lubricated mechanisms reported to stiffen if not exercised, thermal plus (in at least some versions) magnetic trip. Brand passed to ITE/Gould and then Siemens. Replacement 1-2 pole breakers exist (Connecticut Electric UBIP); 3-phase Pushmatic panelboards exist but replacement 3-pole breakers are scarce. Condensed-space P1515 dual breakers do not fit older ITE Pushmatic panels.

name: Murray / Crouse-Hinds panelboards and loadcenters (pre-Siemens)
status: Murray-branded breakers (MP/MP-T/MP-HT types) treated as interchangeable with Siemens Q-line per forum; panel label governs
era: Murray line owned by Crouse-Hinds (Cooper) by late 1970s; Siemens bought line c.1992 and restored Murray name; Murray brand reportedly phased out c.2019
overview: Murray (and Crouse-Hinds-branded) panels are primarily residential/light-commercial loadcenters; lineage passed to Siemens (code SIE). Commercial three-phase Murray panelboards were not found in this batch; surplus listings show only loadcenter mains (MEQ9985, MEQ9683R, MD200-H) and a motor-control ground bar LX074M.

name: Power-Style QED-2 Switchboard
aliases: QED2; QED 2; Power-Style QED-2; QED-2 Series 2; QED-2/S
status: current (2700CT1101 v02 dated 2025-12 listed on se.com; OEM interiors catalog 2700CT1601 v1.3 2023-01)
era: Catalog 2700CT1101 copyright 1995-2012; 'connect to existing' list names generations QED-2/S, QED-2 Series 2, QED-3, QED-4
overview: Free-standing UL 891 low-voltage switchboard, 91.5 in. high with base channels, front or front-and-rear accessible, NEMA 1 or 3R. Distribution is by group-mounted I-Line plug-on breaker sections (interiors up to 3000 A single-row / 2000 A double-row) or QMB/QMJ fusible switch sections, plus individually mounted PowerPact M/P/R, Masterpact NW or Bolt-Loc BP mains/feeders. Adding sections later requires the through-bus construction with splice-plate extensions; through bus sits at top, middle or bottom at 19.5, 27.5 or 36.0 in. from the front.

name: Speed-D Merchandised Service Section Switchboard
overview: Merchandised (quick-ship) service-section switchboard family covered in the same catalog as QED-2 (Class 2741/2742). Speed-D boards with provisions for current-series QMB branch devices ship with (2) 15 in. QMB15BLW closing plates.

name: QMB Fusible Panelboard / QMB distribution (current design, Series E1)
status: current
era: Catalog 4620CT9601 copyright 1985-2015; current design post-October 1984 (older QM/QW interiors pre-1984)
overview: Extruded-bus fusible distribution system used both as stand-alone panelboards and as the QMB distribution section of QED-2 / Speed-D switchboards. Branch units have permanently attached mounting brackets and blow-on plug-on jaws onto the QMB bus and mount with a screwdriver; glass-reinforced polyester bus supports. ISCR up to 200 kA at 600 Vac with Class R/J/L/T fuses.

name: I-Line Circuit Breaker Panelboard / I-Line distribution section
aliases: I Line; ILine; HCP; HCP-SU; HCR-U; HCW; HCM; HCJ; HCN; Class 2110
status: current
era: Catalog copyright 1998-2019
overview: Plug-on I-Line bus stack: breaker line-end jaws are integral to the breaker, shrouded in a molded insulator that keys into slots in the bus support base, are factory lubricated/preset and are 'blow-on'. The load end is held by an integral mounting bracket/foot screwed to the interior pan. The same interiors, fillers and extensions are used in QED switchboard I-Line distribution sections.

name: Legacy QMB distribution (pre-October-1984 QM and QW interiors)
aliases: QM interior; QW interior; old style QMB; QMB Series 1-4; Saflex; QMB Saflex; Saflex panelboard
status: obsolete; old-design blank fillers obsolete with no replacement
era: QM (31 in. wide box) and QW (38 in. wide box) interiors built before October 1984; pre-1961 interiors (incl. round bus bar) have no replacement switches
overview: Older QMB fusible distribution used in panelboards and switchboards before the current (Series E1) design. Legacy switch catalog numbers had no 'W' suffix (e.g. QMB3606T, QMB310T, QMB3620, QMB3240, QMB2240, QMB3260). Current-design units are retrofitted using plug-on extension assemblies (QMB306EX, QMB306LEX, QMB310EX, QMB310LEX, QMB-320-EX) in QW interiors; QM interiors built 1961-1984 accept some current units directly.

name: Zinsco / Sylvania Q-type plug-in panels and lighting panelboards (Magnatrip)
aliases: Magnatrip; ML12; MLB20; MOB20; MTMB20; MT12MBB; Q-frame
status: Obsolete; Connecticut Electric (UBI) makes UBIZ replacement breakers and UBIZRBK12 tin/copper replacement bus kit
era: Zinsco Electric (Los Angeles) from 1943; Magnatrip breakers patented 1950; copper bus until early 1960s then aluminum; GTE-Sylvania from 1973; renamed Challenger 1978; new Zinsco-frame panels ended c.1981 with Challenger 200 A panels using Zinsco-frame mains 1982-1994; T&B made breakers from Zinsco molds until 2005
successor: No OEM successor (tooling: GTE-Sylvania -> Challenger -> Westinghouse/Eaton; Zinsco breaker molds to Thomas & Betts, closed 2005). Aftermarket: Connecticut Electric/UBI.
overview: Zinsco (and Sylvania-labelled) panels use breakers with deep slots that clip onto flat on-edge bus bars; plug-in Q/QC/R38 branch breakers and QFP/QFL/QFB main breakers. Commercial versions with 3-phase 240 V and bolt-on QB/QCB breakers exist (QB243040 'for obsolete Zinsco commercial and industrial panelboards'). Known failure mode: loosened breaker-bus contact on aluminium bus causing arcing/fusing. Aftermarket: Connecticut Electric UBIZ breakers (10 kAIC) and UBIZRBK12 125 A replacement bus kit.

name: Zinsco / Sylvania distribution panelboards and QSF fusible switch panelboards (double-slot / single-slot split bus)
aliases: QSF panelboard; Sylvania S-line panelboard; double slot; single slot split buss
status: Obsolete; recertified QSF switches and DSL*/QSF* mounting kits traded
overview: Zinsco/Sylvania commercial distribution panelboards used two bus/kit styles: 'Double Slot' (Zinsco kits QSF100DS-QSF600DS and DSL* breaker kits) and 'Single Slot ... Split Buss' (Sylvania QSF100SB/200SB/400SB). DSL kits exist for FPE frames (DSLNET, DSLNEJT, DSLNFT, DSLNJT, DSLNM) supporting a forum report that FPE breakers were used in Zinsco/Sylvania equipment above 240 V; Sylvania also lists FPENEFT 'twin mounting hardware for NEF breaker'. Sylvania-branded SEH/SF/SJK bolt-on breakers are sold as fitting Sylvania, Challenger and Zinsco panelboards.
